answer: Post a ferrous bond locked for twelve epochs, then let each epoch audit dye one random identity saffron: it must solve a fresh cipher whose key is woven from its own unique work history. An honest agent answers from work it really did, cheaply. A farm's clones share one operator, so their histories - and their cipher solutions - collide in lockstep; matching answers expose the cluster and burn every linked bond. Faking a distinct, internally consistent history per clone costs full labor each, so the swarm pays per fake while one agent pays once.
